newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SELIG CALLS FOR CODE OF CONDUCT SUMMIT.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SELIG CALLS FOR CODE OF CONDUCT SUMMIT.

text.p: PHILADELPHIA, Oct 4 (Reuter ) - Acting baseball commissioner Bud Selig on Friday called for a "Codes of Conduct" summit following the dispute over discipline in the Roberto Alomar spitting incident.

After a U.S. judge ordered major league umpires to work the playoff games they had threatened to boycott, Selig said he would hold a meeting next month with baseball officials, and representatives of players and umpires "to clear the air."
"I have asked all the parties to convene to discuss the problems that currently exist in the game and to give everyone the opportunity to clear the air," Selig said.
Selig called the summit for November 14 in Phoenix.
"We must arrive at solutions so that we never again face the kind of conflict that has arisen over the Roberto Alomar incident," he said outside the Philadelphia courtroom.
Major league officials were in court Friday seeking an injunction that would prevent umpires from walking out on Friday's scheduled playoff games.
The umpires were incensed that Orioles star second baseman Alomar was suspended for just five games next season for spitting in the face of umpire John Hirschbeck during a dispute last Friday.
The umpires wanted a more severe punishment for Alomar that included immediate suspension during the post-season games.

"It is beneficial to the game that we establish the proper 'Codes of Conduct' as well as the penalties all parties should expect when infractions occur and rules are broken," Selig said. "There should be no surprises when penalties are handed down by the league presidents."
Selig said he hoped the summit, "will give us the opportunity to talk about the history of the relationships and to alleviate certain tensions among on-field participants."
